plan: This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) if I win, bidding exactly my value of $31 maximizes my expected profit - I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids and pay less than my value, and I don't want to risk winning at a price above my value or losing a profitable opportunity. No history exists to suggest deviation from this optimal strategy.

This is a second-price auction format where I pay the second-highest bid if I win. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding higher risks overpaying (winning at a price above my value), while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this is a one-shot game with no repeated learning needed, truthful bidding maximizes my expected profit.

This is a second-price auction format where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid. Bidding exactly my value of $46 ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value exceeds the second-highest bid) and never overpay, since I'd only pay what the next highest bidder offered. This maximizes expected profit in this single-round, independent-value auction.
